assets.title: Assets
assets.subtitle.one: {n} asset in this organization · declaring one never grants a scan: it opens a request in Settings → Grants
assets.subtitle.other: {n} assets in this organization · declaring one never grants a scan: it opens a request in Settings → Grants
assets.empty.title: No assets yet
assets.empty.hint: Declare a domain below, or sweep a seed domain to discover its subdomains.
assets.add.placeholder: add a domain, IP, URL or CIDR
assets.auth.pendingTitle: waiting for an administrator in Settings → Grants
assets.error.notAuthorized: Not authorized for {principal}: a collector runs only on what Grants approved (a simple scan needs passive discovery and active verification). {message}
assets.notice.alreadyCovered: {value} is already covered by an active grant.
assets.notice.excludedFromScope: {value} is excluded from scope: an exclusion wins over any grant.
assets.notice.requestSent: request sent to Grants for {value}. An administrator approves it there and chooses the scope and the actions — declaring never grants a scan.
assets.notice.recordedExcluded: {value} recorded. It is excluded from scope, so nothing was requested.
assets.notice.recordedCovered: {value} recorded. An active grant already covers it.
assets.notice.groupDeleted: deleted group {name}; its assets are untouched
assets.attention.note: Computed from the inventory on every load. Each row names what is missing; “never observed” is a coverage gap, not a statement that the host is gone.
assets.attention.empty.title: Nothing needs attention
assets.attention.empty.hint: Every asset has an owner, a project, a confirmed classification and a deployment relation.
assets.groups.note: Inventory groups organize resources. They are not access groups and grant nobody a permission.
assets.groups.empty.title: No groups yet
assets.groups.empty.hint: Create one for the assets you read together — production domains, a customer estate, an acquisition.
assets.field.name: name
assets.activity.note: The same ledger the Audit trail reads; every row says who, what and when.
assets.activity.empty.title: No activity recorded yet
assets.activity.empty.hint: Adding an asset, editing ownership or moving it between groups writes a row here.
assets.edit.title: Edit {value}
assets.edit.note: Classification records ownership. It is not an authorization: a scan still needs an approved grant in Settings → Grants.
assets.groupDialog.title: New inventory group
assets.detail.collectAsTitle: The identity the grant is issued to. Collection is authorized per principal.
assets.detail.notTrusted: not trusted — see the probe error
assets.detail.techNotCollected: not collected — an advanced scan is what reads versions, banners and ports.
assets.detail.authNote: an approved grant is the only thing that lets a collector touch this host
assets.detail.requestNote: the request lands in Settings → Grants, where an administrator decides the scope and what may be done — that choice is not made here
assets.detail.changes: what changed since the previous observation
assets.fact.subject: subject
assetDetail.notFound.title: asset not found
assetDetail.notFound.hint: it may belong to another workspace
assetDetail.notice.requested: authorization requested — approve it in Settings → Grants
assetDetail.noGrantTitle: nothing can be scanned without a grant
assetDetail.verdict.covered: scans up to {level} are authorized on this asset. Launching one from here still goes through the platform, which re-checks the grant.
assetDetail.verdict.pending: a permission request is waiting in Settings → Grants; nothing can be scanned until it is approved.
assetDetail.verdict.zoneCover: no grant covers this name. {target} is active and covers its subdomains, but a wildcard never covers the apex — request the apex explicitly if this host should be in scope.
assetDetail.verdict.none: no grant covers this asset: declaring it never authorized a scan. Ask for one in Settings → Grants.
assetDetail.fact.subject: subject
assetDetail.services.empty: nothing listening was read — a simple scan resolves the name; services and the stack behind them need the advanced one.
assetDetail.services.unnamed: the port answered, nothing named it
assetDetail.tech.empty: nothing fingerprinted yet — run an advanced scan
attackSurface.title: Attack surface
attackSurface.subtitle: Observed surface and pending ownership decisions · no screen here runs a collector
attackSurface.review.moved: Confirming ownership lives in Assets → Needs attention, where the same assets carry the classification dialog and a note. This screen keeps what the estate publishes and what imitates it.
attackSurface.web.empty.title: No web paths imported
attackSurface.web.empty.hint: Use POST /api/v1/attack-surface/web-endpoints with a crawler or report output. An empty list means no crawling has been imported.
attackSurface.lookalikes.note: passive only: DNS/CT evidence, never an HTTP contact
attackSurface.lookalikes.empty.title: No lookalikes
attackSurface.lookalikes.empty.hint: Import a watched root domain and its candidates; DNS resolving alone is never treated as registration or malice.
attackSurface.review.note: Assets whose ownership is unsettled. Confirming an asset is ours does not authorize testing it, and an IP observed under a domain may belong to a CDN.
attackSurface.review.empty.title: Nothing to review
attackSurface.review.empty.hint: Every asset has a settled ownership decision.
attackSurface.weekly.noChanges: no comparable changes in the window
attackSurface.weekly.notWired: no notification channel and no scheduler are wired for the digest; this endpoint is a query, not a delivery
attackSurface.stateDialog.title: State for {path}
attackSurface.reviewDialog.title: Review {name}
attackSurface.reviewDialog.note: Ownership is inventory truth, not authorization.
attackSurface.lookalikeDialog.note: Lookalikes are never contacted and never added to scope.
scope.title: Scope
scope.subtitle.one: {declared} declared · {active} active · {n} pattern rule · exclusions always win
scope.subtitle.other: {declared} declared · {active} active · {n} pattern rules · exclusions always win
scope.note.before: A row is a declaration: it runs nothing and grants nothing — collectors still need a scan grant.
scope.note.afterPattern: covers subdomains at any depth; the apex only when the row says
scope.capability.permitsTitle: this row permits {capability} — click to withdraw it
scope.capability.disabledTitle: the row is disabled, so nothing here runs
scope.capability.addVerificationTitle: add active verification: this row then also allows probing, not just discovery
scope.apex.coveredTitle: the apex is covered — click to exclude it
scope.apex.uncoveredTitle: the apex is not covered — click to include it
scope.targets.empty.title: Nothing declared yet
scope.targets.empty.hint: Declare the domains, IP ranges and repositories the organization owns. Until you do, the honest answer to “may I test this?” is no.
scope.excl.empty.title: No exclusions
scope.excl.empty.hint: Exclusions cover a value or a pattern and always beat a target that would include it.
scope.notice.alreadyDeclared: that target was already declared; nothing duplicated
scope.notice.declaredRule: declared {type} {value} · rule only, no host created
scope.notice.exclusionAdded: exclusion added; it wins over any target that covers it
scope.check.note: This answers a declaration question only. Running anything still needs a scan grant for the acting principal.
scope.declare.title: Declare a scope target
scope.declare.cloudHint: declarative only: it authorizes no provider address
scope.declare.capabilitiesNote: Recording a capability runs nothing; a scan grant is still required.
scope.exclusion.title: Add a scope exclusion
scope.exclusion.note: Excluding keeps the inventory and does not resolve findings.
jira.title: Jira links
jira.notConfigured: Jira not connected — save the connection in the setup walkthrough (/startup → Tickets), or set JIRA_BASE_URL / JIRA_TOKEN
jira.empty.hint: A link is created from a finding's drawer (Jira button) or with the search below.
jira.searchPlaceholder: search a finding by title, component or id
jira.queued: link queued; the issue was not created yet
jira.note: Jira is the source of truth only for its own workflow. A ticket moved to Done flags the link as verification_required — it never closes the finding.
attackSurface.note.endpoints: a 200 is an observed response, not a vulnerability; excluded paths were not evaluated
assets.map.noGeolocator: no geolocator is configured for this deployment
assets.subdomains.title: subdomains
assets.subdomains.empty: no subdomain is known for this name yet
assets.subdomains.emptyLong: no subdomain is known for this name yet.
scope.declare.searchLabel: Search a target that already exists
scope.declare.searchHint: Only what the inventory already holds or an active grant already names. Pick it instead of typing a second record for the same host.
scope.declare.manualTitle: Or declare something new by hand
scope.declare.pickedUngranted: {value} — in the inventory, no grant covers it yet.
scans.subtitle: Schedule scans, follow every run they produce, and see which workflows they run.
scans.field.name: Scan name
scans.field.targets.hint: Domains, separated by a comma, a space or a new line.
scans.field.schedule.hint: A scan that repeats is a definition; a scan that runs once is a run.
scans.intensity.hint: The intensity is declared by the workflow, not chosen next to it: it is how far the steps may touch the target.
scans.no.workflow.at.level: No workflow declares this intensity. The catalog is the list; nothing is invented here.
scans.options.intro: Runs execute on the platform's workers; the CLI plane is for an operator's own machine and needs owner or admin rights.
scans.options.limit: Whatever a step needs beyond this profile needs a wider grant first.
scans.schedule.once: A one-off scan becomes a run straight away.
scans.review.name: Name
scans.review.note: Nothing is sent until you confirm: the plan above is what the workers will be allowed to do.
scans.approvals.empty.hint: Missions, paused runs and candidates that need a decision land here.
scans.approvals.intro: What the organization's rules stopped and a person has to decide. Scans have no approval gate yet: they are stopped by scope and grants.
scans.empty.title: No scans yet
scans.empty.hint: A scan is a definition: a workflow, a set of targets and how often it repeats.
scans.col.name: Name
scans.runs.empty.hint: A run is what a scan produces — or what you launch once from this page.
scans.no.scope: No target is covered by scope: every step falls outside the grant.
scans.workflows.intro: Catalog workflows come from Shauron and cannot be edited: copy one and it becomes yours. A step can only use tools that exist in the catalog, and the workflow's level limits which of those it may carry.
workflows.mine.empty: You have no workflows of your own yet. Copy one from the catalog, or start from scratch.
workflows.tool.needs: {tool} belongs to {level}: raise the workflow's level to use it
workflows.field.label: Name
workflows.field.level.hint: The level caps which tools the steps may carry. It is the engine's rule, not a suggestion.
workflows.field.question: What does it answer?
workflows.field.question.hint: One sentence an operator reads before launching it.
workflows.field.question.ph: Which hosts answer, and what do they say about themselves?
workflows.field.plane.hint: cloud: the platform's workers. cli: an operator's machine, owners and admins only.
workflows.check.label: Give it a name of at least two characters.
workflows.check.stage_id: Stage {index} needs an id: lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes.
workflows.check.first_stage: The first stage reads from the targets.
workflows.error.bad_slug: That name cannot be used as an identifier: use lowercase letters, numbers, dots or dashes ({at}).
workflows.error.stage_empty: A workflow needs at least one stage.
workflows.error.stage_unknown_from: Stage {stage} reads from {at}, which does not exist yet.
workflows.error.rules_unpublished: The published catalog does not carry the engine's rules: run scripts/sync_surface_catalog.py.
workflows.error.profile_required: Name a profile or one of your workflows.
